A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FlowScene and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite substantial reformatting and relocation; no essential reading gap prevents comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original FlowScene experiments on SemanticKITTI and SSCBench-KITTI-360, including quantitative comparisons, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative predictions.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds backbone-controlled comparisons, category-group analyses, and qualitative cases.

M1.justification: The RepViT/FPN encoder, frozen GMFlow, flow-guided temporal aggregation, occlusion-guided voxel refinement, and training losses are retained. V2's projection equations and Algorithms 1–2 document existing operations rather than establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate outdoor semantic scene completion on SemanticKITTI and SSCBench-KITTI-360. Static/dynamic class aggregation and additional visual cases examine retained coverage. The added ImageNet accuracy column describes pretrained backbones, not a new FlowScene evaluation task.

E2.justification: V2 adds IAMSSC and CGFormer to the KITTI-360 comparison in Table 2, and replaces OccFormer with VLScene in the range comparison in Table 3. Appendix B.1/Table 11 substantially extends comparison methods through RepViT variants of MonoScene, VoxFormer, BRGScene, HTCL, and VLScene.

E3.justification: V2 introduces comparisons using a shared RepViT encoder while retaining each baseline's other settings, separate static/dynamic class-group scoring, and weighted mIoU reporting. These add substantive controls and evaluation measures. The original dataset splits, image resolutions, historical-frame count, and default training recipe remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine motion-related class performance (Table 5), backbone dependence across methods (Table 11), a moving cyclist sequence (Figure 7), and two failure cases (Figure 8). Existing component, temporal-input, optical-flow-network, and backbone ablations are retained. Table 7 reorganizes previously reported scores into an alignment-strategy comparison rather than establishing new runs.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates without uncertainty analysis. V2 Appendix B.2/Table 12 adds weighted standard deviations and standard errors across semantic categories, but supplies no repeated-run or seed information. The checklist still states that error bars are omitted for computational cost; the addition concerns category-level dispersion, not demonstrated run-to-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces FlowScene's KITTI-360 mIoU/IoU of 19.12/46.98 with 20.81/46.95, without explaining a setting change. Newly included CGFormer achieves 48.07 IoU, removing FlowScene's geometric lead in that comparison. New category-group, backbone-controlled, and statistical results substantially expand reported outcomes; SemanticKITTI test and validation mIoU remain 17.70 and 18.13.

T1.justification: V2 explicitly writes voxel-pooling and round-trip flow-consistency formulas for operations already specified in v1. These elaborate the existing mathematics without introducing a substantive new assumption, theoretical result, proof, or changed mathematical procedure.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: optical-flow-guided temporal SSC, the FGTA and OGVR modules, and state-of-the-art performance on the same two benchmarks. Adding explicit mIoU values to the abstract does not change these claims' scope.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the KITTI-360 discussion of superiority in both metrics with emphasis on potentially moving objects, and acknowledges CGFormer's stronger static-class score. It adds interpretations about RepViT's generalizability, claims statistical meaningfulness from class-level dispersion, and identifies dependence on pretrained flow under degraded visual conditions as a limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands implementation documentation through explicit flow-consistency calculations and FGTA/OGVR pseudocode, including cumulative mask union and numerical normalization safeguards. V2 also adds a project-page link and a code-release promise. Existing training and hardware details are relocated unchanged; actual code availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 shortens the general SSC survey and removes several RGBD/LiDAR references, including SSC-RS and SCPNet. It adds VLScene's vision-language positioning and an ImageNet citation. The central relationship to temporal SSC and optical-flow aggregation research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Much of the abstract, introduction, methodology, and conclusion remains verbatim. V2 moves experimental setup to Appendix A, promotes existing optical-flow and backbone ablations into Section 4.3, regroups the supplementary sections, and expands procedural explanations. Author information, acknowledgments, and a conference checklist are also added.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation with widespread resizing and relocation. V2 adds four tables, two algorithm displays, dynamic-sequence and failure-case figures, and an accuracy column to the backbone table. Existing qualitative figures are retained and renumbered; class-frequency annotations are removed from the main benchmark table headers.

improvement.justification: The implementation explanations and backbone-controlled comparisons improve reproducibility and help assess whether advantages depend on encoder choice; failure cases and a specific flow-model limitation improve scrutiny. These gains are tempered by the new statistics section: Table 12 is described as validation analysis but uses FlowScene's test mIoU, and its TPVFormer score matches OccFormer in Table 1. Category-level SD/SE also does not establish the claimed statistical significance. The net improvement is therefore limited.
